newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends near year high on capital inflow.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends near year high on capital inflow.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed firmer for the fifth session in a row on Friday, its strongest level against the dollar since February 20.
Dealers said the peso had closed firmer on capital flows into local markets amid international financial stability.
"Local corporations sold dollars and international players stepped into the local bourse," a dealer said. "International markets were relatively stable, too, which also helped."
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended 3.1 and 2.4 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.7860/7.7890 and 7.7820/7.7880 per dollar.
The 48-hour peso closed near its strongest level for the year at 7.7450 pesos, which it last reached on February 20.
Dealers said the peso could gain further ground from the dollar on yesterday's mild inflation data, which pave the way for future interest rate cuts, and a continuing positive trade balance.
"The market is still long on dollars and a good number of corporations have stepped in," another trader said. "So the trend is for the peso to get stronger, maybe even to the 7.7000-per dollar mark."
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 5.8 centavos firmer at 7.7610/7.7650 per dollar.
